items.name: Neuron
items.desc: one cell that carries a signal. alone, it can't do anything.

items.name: Neuron Pair
items.desc: two neurons touching. the gap between them is a synapse. the worm has about 7,000 of these. you have around 100 trillion.

items.name: Nerve Bundle
items.desc: neurons wired together. touch the worm's nose and this is what makes it back away.

items.name: Nerve Ring
items.desc: the worm's brain is a ring wrapped around its throat. everything it knows passes through here.

final.name: The Worm ★
final.desc: c. elegans. one millimeter long. 302 neurons, every one mapped. in 2014 its wiring was loaded into a lego robot, and the robot moved like a worm.

items.name: Spark
items.desc: 13.8 billion years ago, everything that exists came out of a single point. nobody knows what came before, or if 'before' even means anything.

items.name: Atom
items.desc: the first atoms were almost all hydrogen, the simplest kind. about three quarters of ordinary matter still is.

items.name: Gas Cloud
items.desc: hydrogen drifting in the dark until gravity pulls it into a clump.

items.name: Star
items.desc: an explosion held together by its own gravity. it cooks hydrogen into heavier atoms.

items.name: Galaxy
items.desc: a hundred billion stars or more, turning together. there are hundreds of billions of galaxies.

items.name: Dust
items.desc: the iron in your blood and the calcium in your bones came from stars that exploded before the sun was born.

items.name: Rock
items.desc: dust sticks to dust. then rock hits rock, for millions of years.

items.name: Planet
items.desc: a new world, red-hot from every collision. one of those collisions knocked loose the moon.

items.name: Earth
items.desc: the right distance from its star for water to stay liquid.

final.name: Pale Blue Dot ★
final.desc: in 1990, voyager 1 turned around and photographed earth from six billion kilometers away. it's smaller than a pixel. everyone who has ever lived is in that pixel.

items.name: Cell
items.desc: every living thing that has ever existed descends from one of these.

items.name: Jellyfish
items.desc: no brain, no heart, no bones. jellyfish have been drifting for more than 500 million years.

items.name: Trilobite
items.desc: its eyes had lenses made of crystal. it saw the world through stone.

items.name: Fish
items.desc: everything with a backbone, including you, started as one of these.

items.name: Lizard
items.desc: an egg with a shell meant life could finally leave the water for good.

items.name: Dinosaur
items.desc: they ruled for 165 million years. tyrannosaurus lived closer in time to you than to stegosaurus.

items.name: Eye Spot
items.desc: a patch of cells that can tell light from dark. that's all. that's everything.

items.name: Eye Cup
items.desc: fold the patch inward and now it knows which direction the light came from.

items.name: Eyeball
items.desc: add a lens and the world comes into focus. eyes evolved on their own more than 40 separate times.

final.name: The Eye ★
final.desc: 541 million years ago, the first eyes opened. by the time of the dinosaurs, the world had been watched for 300 million years. it has never stopped.

items.name: Asteroid
items.desc: ten kilometers wide. its orbit and ours were always going to meet.

items.name: Fireball
items.desc: about twenty kilometers per second. it crossed the sky in seconds.

items.name: Crater
items.desc: 180 kilometers wide, buried under mexico. three out of four species didn't survive what came next.

items.name: Ash Cloud
items.desc: soot blocked the sun for years. the world went dark and cold.

items.name: Mouse
items.desc: the mammals that survived were small. they lived underground and came out at night.

items.name: Lemur
items.desc: hands that grip. eyes that face forward.

items.name: Monkey
items.desc: a bigger brain, a longer childhood, a family.

items.name: Ape
items.desc: no tail. around seven million years ago, one line of apes started walking on two legs.

final.name: Footprint ★
final.desc: 3.66 million years ago, two people walked across fresh volcanic ash in tanzania. rain set it like cement. their footprints are still there.

items.name: Baby
items.desc: human babies are born more helpless than almost any other animal. someone has to stay.

items.name: Child
items.desc: learns everything by copying. watch what you teach it.

items.name: Teen
items.desc: a brain rewiring itself. it won't finish until around 25.

items.name: Adult
items.desc: hunts, gathers, carries, remembers where the water is.

items.name: Elder
items.desc: for most of history, the oldest person alive was the whole library.

items.name: Stone Tool
items.desc: 3.3 million years old, older than our species. someone hit a rock with a rock, on purpose.

items.name: Flint
items.desc: strike it against the right stone and you get a spark.

items.name: Fire
items.desc: cooked food is easier to digest. some scientists think fire is why our brains got so big.

items.name: Spear
items.desc: now we could hunt things bigger than us.

items.name: Bone Needle
items.desc: clothes. which meant cold places. which meant everywhere.

items.name: Cave Painting
items.desc: animals in ochre and charcoal, painted by firelight deep inside a cave.

final.name: Handprint ★
final.desc: paint blown around a hand pressed to a cave wall, tens of thousands of years ago. it means: i was here.

items.name: Wheel
items.desc: about 5,500 years ago. first for pottery. then someone turned it on its side.

items.name: Water Wheel
items.desc: the river does the work now.

items.name: Steam Engine
items.desc: boil water, push a piston, change the world.

items.name: Kite
items.desc: 1752. ben franklin flew a kite into a storm to prove lightning was electricity.

items.name: Lightbulb
items.desc: edison's team tested thousands of materials. the one that lasted 1,200 hours was bamboo.

items.name: Clay Tablet
items.desc: writing was invented to keep track of grain and debt. poetry came later.

items.name: Printing Press
items.desc: around 1440. ideas stopped dying with the people who had them.

items.name: Telegraph
items.desc: 1844: 'what hath god wrought.' a message that outran a horse.

items.name: Telephone
items.desc: a voice turned into electricity and back. 'mr. watson, come here, i want to see you.'

items.name: Radio
items.desc: voices through the air. the earliest broadcasts are still traveling out into space.

final.name: The Transistor ★
final.desc: 1947. a switch with no moving parts. it only works because of quantum mechanics. there are billions of them in the phone in your hand.

items.name: Hut
items.desc: four walls and a roof. the first time a place was yours.

items.name: House
items.desc: farming meant staying. staying meant building something that would last.

items.name: Village
items.desc: a few families. everyone knows everyone.

items.name: Town
items.desc: a market, a wall, someone in charge.

items.name: City
items.desc: uruk, 5,000 years ago. the first time that many strangers had to live together.

items.name: Skyscraper
items.desc: steel frames and the elevator made up possible.

items.name: Metropolis
items.desc: more than half of all humans live in cities now. from above at night, they look like circuitry.

items.name: Horse & Buggy
items.desc: for all of history, nothing on land moved faster than a horse.

items.name: Train
items.desc: railroads made the world agree on what time it was.

items.name: Car
items.desc: freedom, traffic, the suburbs, the smell of gasoline.

items.name: Airplane
items.desc: 1903. twelve seconds in the air. sixty-six years later, people walked on the moon.

items.name: Rocket
items.desc: to leave the earth you have to go about eleven kilometers per second.

items.name: Satellite
items.desc: thousands of them overhead right now. one of them is telling your phone where you are.

final.name: Data Center ★
final.desc: rooms full of machines holding everything we've written, posted and searched. they never sleep. some use as much electricity as a small city.

items.name: Baby Bottle
items.desc: a newborn can only focus about 25 centimeters away. just far enough to see the face holding them.

items.name: Pacifier
items.desc: comfort you can hold in your mouth. you'll look for it in other shapes for the rest of your life.

items.name: Building Blocks
items.desc: stack, knock down, stack again. the first physics you ever did.

items.name: Crayons
items.desc: the 64-box with the sharpener built into the back.

items.name: Lunchbox
items.desc: a metal box with a cartoon on the lid and a thermos that always leaked.

items.name: School Bus
items.desc: the same seat every morning. the smell of vinyl and rain.

items.name: Backpack
items.desc: everything important, on your back, every day.

items.name: Trolls Doll
items.desc: first carved by a danish woodcarver in 1959. the neon hair came later.

items.name: Poochi
items.desc: a toy dog that was never going to die. you checked on it anyway.

items.name: Furby
items.desc: it seemed to learn english the more you talked to it. it didn't. it was programmed to seem like it did.

items.name: Tamagotchi
items.desc: a pet that lived on a keychain. if you forgot to feed it, it died. then you pressed reset.

items.name: Game Boy
items.desc: 1989. a grey brick, four AA batteries, and a whole world in green.

items.name: Nintendo 64
items.desc: four controller ports. everyone in the same room, playing the same game.

items.name: PlayStation
items.desc: the memory card held fifteen blocks. you chose which ones to keep.

items.name: Paw Print
items.desc: you didn't tap for this.

items.name: Kitten
items.desc: a kitten's eyes stay closed for the first week or two. then they open.

final.name: Home Video ★
final.desc: a tape labeled in marker. the tv is on, the cat is on the rug, and somebody is laughing off-camera.

extra.name: Cat
extra.desc: in 1935, a physicist imagined a cat sealed in a box, alive and dead at the same time until someone looks. you looked.

items.name: Old Mac
items.desc: a beige box and a startup chime. the first machine in the house that talked back.

items.name: Floppy Disk
items.desc: 1.44 megabytes. it's still the save icon.

items.name: CD
items.desc: a laser reads tiny pits along a spiral. seventy-four minutes of music.

items.name: Flip Phone
items.desc: snake. t9. snapping it shut to hang up on someone.

items.name: Smartphone
items.desc: 2007. the internet in your pocket. you'll touch it thousands of times a day.

items.name: Notification
items.desc: a red dot. your brain treats it like something might be wrong.

items.name: AI Chatbot
items.desc: a machine that writes and talks back. everyone's asking what it means. so is it.

items.name: Breaking News
items.desc: something terrible happened somewhere. it will happen again tomorrow.

items.name: Missed Call (Mom)
items.desc: you'll call her back.

items.name: Overdue Bill
items.desc: red text. you already knew.

items.name: Pill Bottle
items.desc: it helps. it's supposed to.

items.name: Unread Emails
items.desc: 999+. you stopped opening them. they didn't stop coming.

items.name: Layoff Email
items.desc: a calendar invite with no agenda.

items.name: Eviction Notice
items.desc: taped to the door where the whole hallway can read it.

items.name: Tissue Box
items.desc: kept in the car. for the parking lot, before you go inside.

items.name: Group Chat
items.desc: forty people who used to be strangers, all typing at once.

items.name: Union Card
items.desc: a signature. the first one is the hardest. the second one is easier.

items.name: Picket Sign
items.desc: the work stops. for once, someone has to listen.

items.name: Town Hall Chair
items.desc: a folding chair in a fire hall. it's how a town says no.

final.name: Cracked Screen ★
final.desc: the world and the weight, at the same time. something had to give.

items.name: Virus Particle
items.desc: about a ten-thousandth of a millimeter across. not quite alive. it can't do anything until it gets inside you.

items.name: Positive Test
items.desc: two lines.

items.name: Ambulance
items.desc: the sirens didn't stop for weeks.

items.name: Ventilator
items.desc: a machine, breathing for someone.

items.name: Face Mask
items.desc: a thin layer between you and everyone else.

items.name: Hand Sanitizer
items.desc: sold out everywhere. people made it in their kitchens.

items.name: Toilet Paper
items.desc: the shelves were empty. nobody could really explain why.

items.name: Closed Sign
items.desc: cities that never slept went silent. you heard birds you'd never noticed before.

items.name: Video Call
items.desc: everyone you know in little boxes. 'you're on mute.'

items.name: Vaccine Vial
items.desc: made in under a year, on decades of research nobody had heard of.

final.name: Open Sign ★
final.desc: the sign flipped back. you were still here. that counts for something.

items.name: Soldier
items.desc: usually young. usually sent by someone who isn't going.

items.name: Tank
items.desc: sixty tons of steel that can drive through a house.

items.name: Drone
items.desc: the pilot might be on another continent, home in time for dinner.

items.name: Missile
items.desc: it takes seconds.

items.name: Bombed Hospital
items.desc: under the laws of war, a hospital is never supposed to be a target.

items.name: Body
items.desc: a civilian. the silhouette could be anyone.

items.name: Rubble
items.desc: someone's kitchen is in there somewhere.

items.name: Refugee
items.desc: one small bag. what would you grab?

items.name: Tent
items.desc: temporary, for years.

items.name: Aid Crate
items.desc: food falling from the sky. never enough.

items.name: Memorial
items.desc: stone, so no one forgets. people forget anyway.

items.name: Constitution
items.desc: rights, written down. a promise on paper.

items.name: Newspaper
items.desc: someone whose job is to say what happened.

items.name: Protest Sign
items.desc: cardboard and marker. the oldest social media.

items.name: Megaphone
items.desc: one voice, loud enough for a crowd.

items.name: Police Lights
items.desc: red and blue on the ceiling.

items.name: Raised Fist
items.desc: 2020. possibly the largest protest movement in american history.

items.name: Ceasefire Sign
items.desc: one word, painted by people who never fired anything.

items.name: Ballot Box
items.desc: one paper, one vote. people died so you could fold it and drop it in.

final.name: Redrawn Map ★
final.desc: the same world with the borders redrawn. again.

items.name: Handshake
items.desc: two men agree on something in a room you'll never see the inside of.

items.name: Pen
items.desc: gold. used once. given away as a souvenir.

items.name: Signed Pledge
items.desc: a promise to police themselves. nobody can make them keep it.

items.name: Voluntary Stamp
items.desc: one word that means no law, no penalty. trust us.

items.name: Forest
items.desc: old trees, and a hunting lease a family held for generations.

items.name: Fence
items.desc: it went up quietly. the neighbors found out when their leases ended.

items.name: No Hunting Sign
items.desc: the land is protected now. from you.

items.name: Bunker
items.desc: air filters, a year of food, and a door that only opens from the inside.

items.name: Tax Break
items.desc: a billion dollars the county will never collect, so the machine will come here.

items.name: Bonus Check
items.desc: fifty thousand dollars. more than a year's pay. it's hard to argue with.

items.name: Water Meter
items.desc: it spins all night. the aquifer under the farms is feeding it.

items.name: Dry Well
items.desc: the pump hums and nothing comes up.

final.name: Gold Trophy ★
final.desc: first place, in a race to build something smarter than everyone. there was never going to be a second place.

items.name: Get Well Card
items.desc: everyone signed it. nobody knew what to write.

items.name: Flowers
items.desc: the nurses let you keep them by the window.

items.name: Hospital Bed
items.desc: the rails go up at night.

items.name: IV Drip
items.desc: drop by drop. you count them without meaning to.

items.name: Heart Monitor
items.desc: you learn the sound. then you learn to listen for it stopping.

items.name: Flatline
items.desc: hearing may be one of the last senses to go. you kept talking.

items.name: Photograph
items.desc: the version of them you want to keep.

items.name: Reading Glasses
items.desc: still folded on the nightstand.

items.name: Their Sweater
items.desc: it still smells like them. for a while.

final.name: Gravestone ★
final.desc: no name. no date. you know who it is.

items.name: Tea
items.desc: caffeine and warm hands. the gentlest escape.

items.name: Coffee
items.desc: caffeine blocks the chemical that tells your brain it's tired. you're still tired. you just can't feel it.

items.name: Energy Drink
items.desc: a few cups of coffee in a can that looks like a toy.

items.name: Cigarette
items.desc: nicotine reaches the brain in about ten seconds.

items.name: Vape
items.desc: the same thing. it smells like mango.

items.name: Joint
items.desc: time stretches. the song means something now.

items.name: Mushrooms
items.desc: psilocybin quiets the part of the brain that keeps telling you who you are.

items.name: Wire
items.desc: copper. a signal moving at a good fraction of the speed of light.

items.name: Circuit Board
items.desc: a city again. roads for electrons.

items.name: Chip
items.desc: billions of transistors on a sliver of silicon the size of a fingernail.

items.name: Processor
items.desc: it does one simple thing billions of times a second.

items.name: Neural Link
items.desc: electrodes thinner than a hair, listening to neurons as they fire.

items.name: Brain Scanner
items.desc: it maps every connection. the first creature ever fully mapped was a worm.

items.name: Brain
items.desc: about 86 billion neurons. the worm had 302.

final.name: Brain with Wires ★
final.desc: a mind, connected. it can be read. maybe it can be copied. the signal coming off it is shaped like a worm.

items.name: Lab Coat
items.desc: a name tag with the name scratched off.

items.name: Keycard
items.desc: level 3. the door at the end of the hall.

items.name: Cage
items.desc: clean. labeled. a water bottle, half full.

items.name: Operating Table
items.desc: sterile, white, too big for what's lying on it.

items.name: The Implant
items.desc: 96 electrodes, smaller than an aspirin. it recorded every signal it could hear.

items.name: Consent Form
items.desc: signed by someone. not by the one it was about.

items.name: Brain Scan
items.desc: a cat's brain, sliced into light.

items.name: Cassette Tape
items.desc: hours of signal. cats dream. this one did.

items.name: Hard Drive
items.desc: everything it ever thought, on one drive.

items.name: Storage Box
items.desc: unlabeled. shelf nine. nobody has opened it in years.

final.name: Sealed Box ★
final.desc: someone kept it. they never said why.

items.name: Bit
items.desc: one or zero. everything you are could be written in these.

items.name: Byte
items.desc: eight bits. enough for one letter.

items.name: Line of Code
items.desc: an instruction. something is writing you back.

items.name: Cursor
items.desc: blinking. waiting for the next thing you'll be.

items.name: Window
items.desc: a program that's running right now. is this one you?

items.name: Loading Bar
items.desc: almost there. it's been almost there for a long time.

items.name: Torn Photo
items.desc: a piece of a memory. you're not sure whose.

items.name: Faded Photo
items.desc: every time you remember something, you rebuild it. it comes out a little different each time.

items.name: Face
items.desc: you know this face. you can't place it.

items.name: Name Tag
items.desc: yours. you'd almost forgotten.

items.name: Mirror
items.desc: the part of you that says 'i'. nobody has found where it lives.

final.name: The String ★
final.desc: string theory says the smallest thing in the universe is a tiny vibrating string. this one looks exactly like the spark that started everything. except for one pixel.

open: yes. his name is in the epstein files.
yes. it's mostly us. greenhouse gases.
